findings.title: Retry cleanup deletes non-SMS and already-scheduled workflow reminders
findings.body: The new OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and no `scheduled: false` condition. The surrounding `deleteMany` therefore deletes every WorkflowReminder row with `retryCount > 1`, including EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders, and it can delete a reminder that is already successfully scheduled. The retry limit is intended only for failed SMS scheduling, so this can silently remove unrelated reminders. Scope the retry-count branch to SMS (and typically unscheduled) reminders.

findings.title: retryCount is incremented via non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: Both failure paths update the row with `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, where `reminder.retryCount` was read at the start of the cron run. If two cron invocations overlap, both can read the same value and write the same increment, losing failures. A reminder can then remain unscheduled for the entire 7-day window without ever reaching the deletion threshold, and overlapping runs can still send duplicate SMS. Use an atomic increment such as Prisma's `{ increment: 1 }`.

findings.title: Errors in the catch-block update abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The new `await prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` inside the `catch` is not itself protected. If the row has been deleted by another concurrent cron run (the new `deleteMany` can delete rows with `retryCount > 1`) or the database update fails, this rejection escapes the per-reminder catch, stops the loop, prevents all remaining reminders from being processed, and makes the cron endpoint fail. Wrap the recovery update or use `updateMany` so one bad row cannot abort the run.

findings.title: Missing sendTo or empty message never increments retryCount
findings.body: The retry increment only happens when `twilio.scheduleSMS` is called and returns falsy or throws. If `sendTo` is missing or `message` is empty, the `if (message?.length && sendTo)` block is skipped entirely, so `retryCount` stays at 0 and the reminder is re-fetched on every cron run until its scheduled date passes. These are exactly the kinds of unschedulable reminders the retry limit is meant to stop retrying, so they should also be counted/deleted or otherwise marked as failed.

findings.title: retryCount cleanup has no supporting index
findings.body: The new `deleteMany` predicate `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` is not covered by any index on WorkflowReminder. Because this cleanup runs on every cron invocation and the OR includes an unindexed predicate, the database may scan the entire WorkflowReminder table repeatedly. Add an index on `retryCount` (or a partial index for the rows the cron needs) to keep the cron cheap as the table grows.

findings.title: No tests cover the retry-count lifecycle or deletion scope
findings.body: The PR changes failure handling and adds destructive cleanup logic but adds no automated tests. There should be coverage for: incrementing on scheduling failure, deleting only after the intended number of failures, not deleting non-SMS reminders, not deleting successfully scheduled reminders, and handling missing `sendTo`/empty `message` failures. Without these, regressions in the retry threshold or accidental cross-method deletion will not be caught.
